newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Pioneer Hi-Bred EPS cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Pioneer Hi-Bred EPS cut.

text.p: Prudential Securities analyst John McMillin said Wednesday he cut his earnings estimates for seed and agricultural genetics company Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc to $2.90 a share from $3.00.
-- His rating on the stock remains hold.
-- Earlier, Pioneer said it expected fiscal 1997 earnings to be "toward the middle" of an estimate range of $2.70 to $3.10 a share, compared with $2.68 earned in fiscal 1996.
-- Pioneer shares were off $5.00 to $71.25 a share, a drop that McMillin attributed in part to the company's forecast of lower-than-expected North American seed corn market share.
-- Pioneer said its 1997 North American seed corn market share is expected to be 42 to 42.5 percent, down one-and-a-half to two points.
-- "I was taken aback by the...decline," McMillin said, adding Pioneer's seed corn market share was expected to drop by only one-half to one point.
-- Pioneer said its North American corn market share was affected by many factors, including transition to a new lineup of crop genetics.

-- The analyst added Pioneer's stock also was pressured by the company's projection that fourth quarter results may not match the previous two years because late planting in 1995 and 1996 delayed some sales to the fourth quarters in those years.
-- McMillin said he still considers Pioneer a "premium company that I think should be attractive long term."
-- "But a lot of fund managers (investors) don't want to wait until next year," he added.
